most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Severe acute Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) with pneumonia, hepatitis, thrombocytopenia, AKI and shock, likely from aerosol exposure while handling a bandicoot carcass; the main alternative is melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei) with a splenic abscess
one_line_reason: In Far North Queensland, handling a bandicoot carcass without a mask, followed two weeks later by fever, pneumonia, hepatitis, thrombocytopenia, AKI, hepatosplenomegaly, confusion and shock, points to a zoonosis caught by breathing it in. That most likely means Q fever. The splenic lesion in a smoker keeps melioidosis (a bacterial sepsis) and leptospirosis close behind.
